Method of Attack: Information-stealing trojan distributed under malware-as-a-service (MaaS) model
Steals stored browser credentials, credit cards, cryptocurrency wallets, email data, and other sensitive data from numerous applications
Discoverer: law enforcement partners in the Netherlands and Italy
Impacted Systems: Infected devices including browsers, cryptocurrency wallets, email clients, and various applications
Attack Vector: Malware-as-a-service subscription allowing threat actors to rent and customize malware
Distribution of trojan malware to victim devices
Indicators of Compromise: Admin panel access for subscribers to retrieve stolen data and create new malware builds
More than 50 million unique credentials and forms of identification stolen
Over four million email addresses identified in stolen data
FBI Raccoon Infostealer Disclosure portal for checking compromised data
